examples.en: The child keeps following me, holding on to my waistband.
Grandfather slipped his hand into his waistband.
Don't walk with your hands in your waistband.
My younger brother's pants keep slipping, so he keeps pulling them up.
The water was deep, so I got wet all the way up to my waist.
A few coins fell out of my waistband.

explain: '허리춤'과 거의 같게 쓰지만 바지의 허리 부분을 가리켜요. '바지춤을 올리다', '바지춤에 손을 넣다'처럼 허리를 잡거나 올리는 동작과 자주 같이 나와요.
explain_en: It is nearly the same as '허리춤' but points to the waist part of pants. It often appears with actions like pulling up the waistband or putting a hand in it, as in '바지춤을 올리다' and '바지춤에 손을 넣다'.

examples.en: A long stick got caught in the bicycle spokes.
One spoke broke, so I went to the repair shop.
The wind whooshes through the spokes.
The old cart had its spokes made of wood.
The sunlight spread out in all directions like spokes.
If you attach a reflector to each spoke, it is safer at night.

explain: 자전거나 수레 바퀴에서 가운데 축과 바깥 테를 이어 주는 가는 막대예요. 자전거 쪽에서는 '스포크'라고도 말해요. '햇살이 바큇살처럼 퍼지다'처럼 한 점에서 사방으로 뻗는 모양을 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: These are the thin rods connecting the hub and the rim of a bicycle or cart wheel. In cycling people also say '스포크' (spoke). It can also describe something spreading out from one point, as in 'light spreading like spokes'.

examples.en: Election day is close, so the candidates are very busy.

examples.ko: 마감이 박두했는데 아직 반도 못 썼어요.
examples.en: The deadline is right around the corner and I haven't even written half.
When exams are imminent, there are no seats in the library.

examples.ko: 새 영화 개봉이 박두해서 벌써 기대돼요.
examples.en: The new movie's release is near, so I'm already excited.
The news says the day of the decisive match is near.
The closer a crisis gets, the calmer you need to be.

explain: 날짜나 사건이 바로 코앞에 닥쳤을 때 쓰는 글말투예요. 일상 대화에서는 '다가오다'나 '코앞이다'라고 말하는 경우가 많아요. 주로 선거, 마감, 개봉처럼 정해진 날이 있는 일과 함께 써요.
explain_en: This is a formal, written-style word for when a date or event is right around the corner. In daily talk people often say '다가오다' or '코앞이다' instead. It mostly goes with things that have a set date, such as elections, deadlines and releases.

en: with a scratching sound; with scrape

examples.en: You have to rub the sleeves hard to get the dirt out.
I scrubbed the soles of my sneakers hard with a toothbrush.
I scrubbed the bottom of the pot hard with a scouring pad.
My head itched, so I scratched it hard.
My hands are dirty, so I'm scrubbing them hard with soap.
There was a sound of someone scraping the wallpaper off.

explain: 힘을 주어 문지르거나 긁거나 씻을 때 나는 소리와 모양이에요. 반대로 부드럽게 할 때는 '살살'이라고 해요. '빡빡'은 더 세고 거친 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It imitates the sound and look of rubbing, scratching or washing with force. The opposite, for gentle action, is '살살'. '빡빡' feels even stronger and rougher.

examples.ko: 그분은 팔자가 박복하다는 말을 자주 들었어요.
examples.en: She often heard people say that her fate was unlucky.
Mother says she had a hard life because she was unlucky.
Don't think you were born unlucky.
Working all your life, you really have bad luck.

examples.ko: 할머니는 젊어서 남편을 잃고 박복했다고 한숨을 쉬셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother sighed that she had been unlucky, losing her husband young.

examples.ko: 박복한 신세를 한탄하는 인물이 드라마에 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Characters who lament their unlucky lot often appear in dramas.

explain: 주로 '팔자', '신세', '인생'처럼 삶 전체를 말하는 단어와 같이 써요. 일상에서는 '운이 없다', '복이 없다'를 더 많이 말해요. 반대는 '복이 많다'이고, 다른 사람에게 직접 말하면 실례가 될 수 있어요.
explain_en: It usually goes with words about life as a whole, such as '팔자', '신세' and '인생'. In daily talk people say '운이 없다' or '복이 없다' more often. The opposite is '복이 많다', and saying it directly to someone can be rude.

examples.en: Despite the low pay, he likes his job.
A new hire's salary is so low that life is tight.

examples.ko: 박봉으로 아이 셋을 키우기가 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It isn't easy to raise three kids on a low salary.
My father struggled with low pay all his life.

examples.ko: 박봉이지만 보람 있는 일이라서 계속 다녀요.
examples.en: The pay is low, but the work is rewarding, so I keep going.

examples.ko: 박봉을 받는 사람들을 위한 지원이 필요해요.
examples.en: Support is needed for people who receive low pay.

explain: 월급이 적다는 뜻을 한 단어로 말하는 표현이에요. '박봉에 시달리다', '박봉이다'처럼 쓰고, 반대는 '고액 연봉'이에요. 구어로는 '월급이 짜다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It packs 'the salary is small' into one word. It is used as '박봉에 시달리다' or '박봉이다', and the opposite is '고액 연봉' (a high annual salary). In casual speech people also say '월급이 짜다'.

en: close contest; narrow margin (lit. thin ice)

examples.ko: 이번 선거는 박빙이라 결과를 알 수 없어요.
examples.en: This election is so close that the result is unpredictable.
The two teams played a nail-biting match.
The score was so close that I was tense until the end.

examples.ko: 여론 조사에서 두 후보가 박빙으로 나왔어요.
examples.en: In the poll, the two candidates came out neck and neck.

examples.ko: 결승전은 박빙 승부 끝에 연장전으로 갔어요.
examples.en: The final went to overtime after a very tight match.
It's neck and neck right now, so who will win?

explain: 사전 뜻은 '얇은 얼음'이지만 요즘은 거의 점수나 표 차이가 아주 작은 경기·선거에 써요. '박빙의 승부', '박빙으로 이기다'처럼 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 비슷한 말로 '접전', '막상막하'가 있어요.
explain_en: The dictionary meaning is 'thin ice', but today it is used almost only for games or elections where the gap in score or votes is tiny. It appears often in news, as in '박빙의 승부' and '박빙으로 이기다'. Similar words are '접전' and '막상막하'.

examples.ko: 우리 선생님은 역사에 대해 정말 박식하세요.
examples.en: Our teacher is really knowledgeable about history.

examples.ko: 박식한 사람과 이야기하면 배울 게 많아요.
examples.en: When you talk with a knowledgeable person, there is a lot to learn.

examples.ko: 그는 커피에 박식해서 추천을 잘해 줘요.
examples.en: He knows a lot about coffee, so he gives good recommendations.

examples.ko: 박식하다는 평을 듣지만 잘난 척하지 않아요.
examples.en: He is said to be well read, but he doesn't show off.
Grandfather is so knowledgeable that there is nothing he doesn't know.
You're so knowledgeable, so why do you say you don't know?

explain: 책이나 공부로 폭넓게 지식을 쌓은 사람에게 하는 칭찬이에요. 보통 '~에 박식하다'처럼 '에'와 함께 쓰고, 높일 때는 '박식하시다'예요. '해박하다'도 비슷한 뜻으로 쓰여요.
explain_en: It is a compliment for someone who has built up wide knowledge through books or study. It is usually used as '~에 박식하다', and the honorific is '박식하시다'. '해박하다' is a similar word.

examples.ko: 그는 박애 정신으로 어려운 사람들을 도왔어요.
examples.en: He helped people in need with a spirit of universal love.
I donated to an organization that puts philanthropy into practice.

examples.ko: 인종을 가리지 않는 박애의 마음이 필요해요.
examples.en: We need a heart of universal love that doesn't discriminate by race.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 박애주의자라서 낯선 사람도 잘 도와줘요.
examples.en: He is a humanitarian, so he helps even strangers.

examples.ko: 이 책은 박애와 평화에 대해 말해요.
examples.en: This book talks about universal love and peace.
Liberty, equality and fraternity is the motto of France.

explain: 모든 사람을 차별 없이 사랑한다는 윤리적·사회적인 말이에요. 보통 '박애 정신', '박애주의'처럼 쓰고, 개인적인 사랑을 말할 때는 쓰지 않아요. 돈이나 물건을 주는 '자선'과 달리 마음의 태도를 가리켜요.
explain_en: It is an ethical and social word for loving all people without discrimination. It is usually used as '박애 정신' or '박애주의' and not for personal love. Unlike '자선' (charity, giving money or goods), it points to an attitude of the heart.

examples.ko: 그는 의지가 박약해서 운동을 금방 포기해요.
examples.en: He is weak-willed, so he gives up exercising quickly.
It is hard to believe a claim with weak grounds.
I was told that my logic was weak.

examples.ko: 의지가 박약했던 때도 있었지만 지금은 달라요.
examples.en: There was a time I was weak-willed, but now I'm different.
This paper was judged to have weak evidence.

examples.ko: 박약해 보이는 논리는 질문을 받으면 무너져요.
examples.en: A weak-looking argument falls apart when you ask questions.

explain: '의지', '근거', '논리'처럼 힘이 있어야 하는 것이 약할 때 써요. 일상에서는 그냥 '약하다'라고 하고, '박약하다'는 글이나 발표에서 많이 나와요. 사람의 지능을 가리키는 말로는 쓰지 마세요.
explain_en: It is used when something that should be strong, like will, evidence or logic, is weak. In daily talk people simply say '약하다', and '박약하다' shows up more in writing and presentations. Do not use it to describe a person's intelligence.

examples.en: Everyone burst into hearty laughter at the comedy act.
The whole family roars with laughter at my friend's joke.
The sound of roaring laughter was heard in the next room.
It was a story so funny that even the teacher would roar with laughter.
It was so funny that I laughed out loud until tears came.

examples.ko: 그 장면을 떠올리면 박장대소할 수밖에 없어요.
examples.en: When I think of that scene, I can't help but burst out laughing.

explain: 손뼉을 치면서 크게 웃는다는 한자 그대로의 모습이 떠오르는 말이에요. 여럿이 함께 있을 때 잘 어울려요. '폭소하다'는 웃음이 갑자기 터지는 데 초점이 있고, '박장대소하다'는 크게 웃는 모습 자체에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: It brings to mind the literal picture of clapping while laughing loudly, and it fits best when several people are together. '폭소하다' focuses on laughter suddenly bursting out, while '박장대소하다' focuses on the picture of laughing big.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 박진감이 넘쳐서 시간이 빨리 갔어요.
examples.en: This movie is so thrilling that time flew by.

examples.ko: 박진감 있는 경기라서 끝까지 숨죽이고 봤어요.
examples.en: It was such an exciting game that I watched it holding my breath.
The music adds a sense of excitement to the scene.
It has a lot of excitement, but the story is a little weak.

examples.ko: 박진감에 빠져서 시간 가는 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I got caught up in the thrill and lost track of time.
The director captivated the audience with intensity.

explain: 영화, 경기, 게임이 생생하고 빠르게 진행되어 실제처럼 느껴질 때 써요. '박진감 넘치다', '박진감이 있다'가 자주 쓰여요. '긴장감'은 조마조마한 마음이고, '박진감'은 장면이 살아 움직이는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used when a movie, game or match moves fast and vividly so it feels real. Common forms are '박진감 넘치다' and '박진감이 있다'. '긴장감' is the nervous feeling, while '박진감' is the sense that the scene is alive and moving.

examples.en: My grandfather is very learned, so he knows everything.
Thanks to our learned teacher, the class is fun.
That writer is famous for being widely learned.
My friend called me widely learned, and I felt shy.
He may look learned, but there are many fields he doesn't know.
I think being widely learned is not the same as being wise.

explain: 학문이 넓고 아는 것이 많다는 사자성어예요. 보통 '박학다식하다', '박학다식한'처럼 형용사처럼 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '아는 게 많다'나 '척척박사'라고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: This four-character idiom means being broadly learned and knowing a lot. It is usually used like an adjective, as in '박학다식하다' and '박학다식한'. In daily talk people also say '아는 게 많다' or '척척박사'.

examples.en: I remember the smooth, shiny scar on his chest.
I just wiped the floor with wax, and it's gleaming.

examples.ko: 비 온 뒤 나뭇잎이 반들거리며 빛났어요.
examples.en: After the rain, the leaves glistened.

examples.ko: 오래 쓴 손잡이가 반들거려서 정이 가요.
examples.en: The handle, worn smooth from long use, is shiny and I feel attached to it.
The slide the kids had used for a long time was polished smooth.
I feel good when my shoe tips shine in the sunlight.

explain: 표면이 매끈해서 윤이 나고 빛이 비칠 때 써요. '반짝거리다'는 빛이 깜빡이듯 빛나는 느낌이고, '반들거리다'는 매끄러운 표면에서 윤이 나는 느낌이에요. 오래 만져서 매끈해진 것에도 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used when a surface is smooth and glossy so that light reflects off it. '반짝거리다' feels like light twinkling, while '반들거리다' feels like a smooth surface with a sheen. It also suits things that have become smooth from long handling.

examples.en: The wooden floor at home is so glossy that it's a little slippery.
I picked out a shiny apple.
There is a chair worn smooth and shiny by hands.
The pebbles have been washed by the river and are smooth.
I feel good when my new shoes are shiny.
My face is reflected in the mirror I polished until it shone.

explain: 표면이 매끄럽고 윤이 나는 모습이에요. '반질반질'과 거의 같게 쓰고, 반대는 '거칠거칠하다'예요. 큰 느낌의 '번들번들'은 기름기가 번지르르할 때 많이 써서 얼굴에 쓰면 좋지 않게 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a smooth, glossy surface. It is used almost the same as '반질반질', and the opposite is '거칠거칠하다' (rough). The bigger-feeling '번들번들' often means greasy-shiny, so using it about a face can sound negative.

examples.en: The books are lined up neatly on the bookshelf.
The child's handwriting is neat and straight, so it's easy to read.
I walked along the straight, orderly road.
The desks in the classroom look lined up in neat rows.
I feel good when the inside of the closet is neatly arranged.
It is a village known for its neatly squared fields.

explain: 여러 개가 모두 곧고 바르게 정돈된 모습에 써요. '반듯하다'는 하나의 물건이나 사람의 행실이 바를 때도 쓰지만, '반듯반듯하다'는 여러 개가 줄지어 있을 때 잘 어울려요. 반의어는 '삐뚤빼뚤하다'예요.
explain_en: It describes many things that are all straight and neatly arranged. '반듯하다' can also be used for a single object or a person's proper behavior, but '반듯반듯하다' fits best when many things are lined up. The opposite is '삐뚤빼뚤하다' (crooked).

examples.en: Try lying straight on the hard floor.

examples.ko: 허리를 펴고 반듯이 앉아야 건강에 좋아요.
examples.en: It is good for your health to sit up straight with your back stretched.
If you fold the paper straight, it looks nice.
He stood up straight and greeted us.

examples.ko: 줄이 반듯이 맞아야 사진이 잘 나와요.
examples.en: The line has to be straight for the photo to come out well.
I placed the desk squarely against the wall.

explain: '반듯이 눕다/앉다/서다'처럼 자세를 나타내는 동사와 자주 나와요. '반드시'와 소리가 같아서 받아쓰기에서 많이 틀려요. 말할 때는 '똑바로'나 '반듯하게'가 더 흔해요.
explain_en: It often goes with posture verbs, as in '반듯이 눕다/앉다/서다'. It sounds the same as '반드시', so it is often misspelled in dictation. In speech, '똑바로' or '반듯하게' is more common.

examples.ko: 우리나라는 반만년의 역사를 가졌다고 자주 말해요.
examples.en: People often say that our country has a history of five thousand years.

examples.ko: 반만년 동안 이어진 풍습이 지금도 남아 있어요.
examples.en: Customs that continued for five thousand years still remain today.
It is a tradition that has lasted five thousand years, so it's really amazing.

examples.ko: 반만년을 이어 온 노래를 함께 불러 봐요.
examples.en: Let's sing together a song that has been passed down for five thousand years.

examples.ko: 반만년간 이 땅에서 살아온 사람들을 생각해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's think about the people who have lived on this land for five thousand years.

examples.ko: 국어 시간에 반만년 역사에 대한 글을 읽었어요.
examples.en: In Korean class, I read an essay about a five-thousand-year history.

explain: 말 그대로 5천 년인데, 한국 역사를 말할 때 '반만년 역사'라고 관용적으로 많이 써요. 정확한 숫자를 따질 때보다 오래된 역사를 자랑스럽게 말할 때 어울려요. '반'은 '만 년의 절반'이에요.
explain_en: It literally means five thousand years, and it is commonly used in the fixed phrase '반만년 역사' when talking about Korean history. It fits proudly describing a long past more than stating an exact number. The '반' means half of ten thousand years.

examples.ko: 그 실수를 반면교사로 삼아 다시는 안 해요.
examples.en: I use that mistake as a lesson and never do it again.
I prepared, taking my senior's failure as a negative example.

examples.ko: 이 사례는 반면교사가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: This case can serve as a lesson on what not to do.

examples.ko: 나쁜 습관을 가진 친구는 제게 반면교사였어요.
examples.en: A friend with bad habits was a cautionary example for me.
This accident is a good example of learning from what went wrong.

examples.ko: 싸우는 모습을 보고 반면교사라는 말을 떠올렸어요.
examples.en: Seeing them fight, I remembered the word 'banmyeongyosa'.

explain: '반면교사로 삼다' 꼴로 거의 굳어서 써요. '타산지석'은 남의 좋은 말과 행동에서도 배울 때 쓰지만, '반면교사'는 나쁜 모습에만 써요. 따라 배울 좋은 본보기는 '귀감'이에요.
explain_en: It is nearly fixed in the form '반면교사로 삼다'. '타산지석' can also be used when learning from others' good words and actions, but '반면교사' is used only for bad examples. A good example to follow is '귀감'.

examples.en: The government issued a rebuttal to the article.
The company's rebuttal was posted online.

examples.ko: 반박문에는 숫자와 사실이 정확히 들어가야 해요.
examples.en: A rebuttal must include accurate numbers and facts.

examples.ko: 반박문은 짧고 분명하게 쓰는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It is best to write a rebuttal briefly and clearly.
He stated his opinion in a long rebuttal.

examples.ko: 이 반박문 때문에 논쟁이 더 커졌어요.
examples.en: The argument grew bigger because of this rebuttal.

explain: '반박'은 일상에서도 쓰지만 '반박문'은 상대 주장이 틀렸다는 입장을 글로 낸 것이에요. 보통 '반박문을 내다/발표하다/올리다'처럼 쓰고, 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. '해명문'은 사정을 설명하는 글이라서 서로 달라요.
explain_en: '반박' is used in daily life too, but '반박문' is a written statement arguing that the other side's claim is wrong. It is used as '반박문을 내다', '발표하다' or '올리다', and appears often in news. A '해명문' explains circumstances, so it is different.
